name: Dendrite Folklore
description:
Dendrite Folklore emerges from the practice of encoding ancestral memory fragments directly into musical compositions via BCI extraction protocols. Performers harvest genuine emotional and sensory memories from elderly citizens—grandparents who remember pre-megacity landscapes, refugees who carry lost cultures in their nervous systems—and weave these raw neural impressions into acoustic and synthetic instrumentation. The result is music that doesn't merely evoke nostalgia but literally transmits it, listeners experiencing secondhand memories of rain on soil, open markets, or family meals that may no longer exist anywhere in physical GLMZ.

The genre occupies a complicated ethical space, as the sourcing of memory material requires consent frameworks that are frequently contested in lower tiers where economic desperation can pressure donors. Authentic Dendrite Folklore is distinguished from its exploitative counterparts by the presence of living donor credits in the track metadata, and purists refuse to engage with anonymous-source compositions. Instruments of choice include resonance harps tuned to brainwave frequencies and modified string ensembles that can carry layered neural data beneath audible melody.
creator: various
tier_availability: All tiers; authentic donor-credited releases concentrated in Tiers 2-4, bootleg extractions prevalent in Tiers 6-8
legality: Legal with donor consent documentation; unconsented memory extraction illegal under Neural Privacy Statutes 44-C
audience: Cultural preservation communities, diaspora populations, memory archivists, elderly citizens seeking connection to younger generations
cultural_impact: Dendrite Folklore has become one of the primary vehicles through which pre-megacity culture survives in GLMZ, functioning simultaneously as art form and living archive. It has generated significant legal reform around neural consent and sparked a broader movement advocating for the rights of memory donors, who some activists argue are the true authors of any work containing their extracted impressions. In upper tiers, sanitized commercial versions stripped of authentic neural data—sometimes called Hollow Folk by critics—have diluted the genre's reputation while making it mainstream.
story_hooks: A memory donor discovers their most private grief has been sampled in a chart-topping commercial track without their knowledge
A Dendrite Folklore archivist finds a memory fragment in an anonymous track that appears to document a crime that was officially ruled an accident
Two competing artists claim the same elderly donor as the source of a foundational memory that defines their careers
